source.title: Lost in the Non-convex Loss Landscape: How to Fine-tune the Large Time Series Model?
source.authors: Xu Zhang; Peng Wang; Wei Wang

record.tranche_reason: Reports fine-tuning and test-performance results on large time-series models, a new setting for the broad generalization topic; it does not test any listed version directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports time-series fine-tuning performance and overfitting, but does not test random-label memorization, the listed architecture/optimizer/batch/regularization/size comparisons, or magnitude-aware sharpness. Its interpolation coefficient and initialization ablations are method settings, not results on a listed version.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates weight interpolation before time-series fine-tuning, but its results test none of V1–V8. Its Hessian-based arguments and landscape visualizations do not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or its ranking of generalization gaps (V7). A new application setting alone does not establish T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record fairly paraphrases the authors' interpretation: steep, irregular pretrained loss landscapes hinder fine-tuning, and interpolation with random initialization improves trainability while preserving pretrained knowledge. The causal explanation and knowledge preservation are the authors' interpretations of their analyses and performance results, rather than independently established mechanisms.
record.recipe_differences: The study interpolates pre-trained and randomly initialized time-series model weights before fine-tuning, and evaluates time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, and imputation rather than the listed classification generalization setups.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to interpolation coefficient and to the proportion of parameters interpolated: preferred parameter proportions vary with dataset size. It reports stable gains across tested initialization schemes and random seeds.

fits_no_version.finding: Direct Timer fine-tuning has the lowest training loss according to Figure 9's accompanying text, yet higher test MSE than training from scratch on ETTh1, ETTm1, and Weather at 100% data.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained time-series models can attain lower downstream training loss yet worse test performance than the same architecture trained from scratch.

record.problems: The qualitative training-loss and test-MSE comparison in Figure 9 has no numerical values in the supplied text. The experiments concern time-series tasks and do not measure generalization gaps in the settings specified by the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows extracted: the other reported forecasting, anomaly-detection, imputation, and zero-shot results compare time-series methods or metrics but do not test a listed version or directly measure the train-test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the paired natural-label versus random-label held-out comparison.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning; Adam is used without this comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe changes that alleviate them.
Dropout effects, including dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Generic flatness–generalization reasoning motivates the method, but does not establish use or testing of V7's specific magnitude-aware measure. No version-level verdict is warranted. Other method comparisons are already declared in rows_left_out.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label held-out accuracy comparison.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected image-model comparison.
No adaptive optimizer comparison; Adam is used in the fine-tuning setup.
No magnitude-aware perturbation measure or comparison of its ranking of generalization gaps.

rows.subject: Timer
rows.operation_detail: Direct full fine-tuning compared with training from scratch on forecasting datasets; paper reports training loss and test MSE qualitatively.

conditions.value: ETTh1, ETTm1, and Weather examples; 100% available data

rows.baseline: Training from scratch; test MSE is described as the reference comparison.
rows.value: Direct fine-tuning had the significantly lowest training loss, but its test MSE was significantly worse than training from scratch on the stated example datasets.
rows.note: The paper does not provide the plotted numerical values in the supplied text, and these time-series results do not measure a listed version.
rows.check: The qualitative comparison accurately reflects Appendix A.5.5, but combines three datasets and two measures and bears on no listed version. Although Figure 9's training-loss values are unavailable, test MSE values are supplied in Tables 1 and 17: FF versus training from scratch is 0.3709 versus 0.3600 on ETTh1, 0.3128 versus 0.3093 on ETTm1, and 0.1612 versus 0.1526 on Weather, at 100% data. The authors describe these differences as significant without reporting a significance test.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
